first.rationale: Competitor entry pricing creates an immediate acquisition risk in the price-sensitive SMB segment, where inherited evidence indicates targeted promotional pricing has lifted qualified acquisition and revenue. A small, tightly targeted test is preferable to a broad discount because activation and onboarding declines may also constrain durable value; those competing explanations should remain open pending verification. Guardrails should assess qualification, post-promotion retention, expansion, and margin rather than acquisition alone.

mid.rationale: Run a standard experiment simplifying onboarding. The verified prior result directly addresses the 4% completion decline and improved completion (+13%), time-to-value (-2.1 days), and 30-day retention (+3%), making it the strongest sustainable-value option. Do not use promotional pricing: verification shows that its acquisition and qualified-revenue gains came with a 12% 30-day retention decline. Track first meaningful action, activation, qualified conversion, retention, and account quality because the prior retention window remains limited.

final2.rationale: Proceed with onboarding simplification rather than a reactive discount. The verified onboarding result improved completion, time-to-value, and 30-day retention, directly addressing current onboarding and activation deterioration. The deeper competitor cut and doubled churn conversations increase urgency, but they do not establish that promotional pricing will sustainably retain existing SMB accounts; the verified pricing experiment produced a 12% 30-day retention decline in the acquired cohort. Measure SMB activation, first meaningful action, qualified conversion, retention, and churn signals by price-sensitivity segment.
